name: page-tint-follows-the-page
description: With chromePageTint on, the chrome drifts toward the active page's declared colour, so switching from a crimson page to a teal one repaints the sidebar backdrop. The two fixture pages declare theme-color and nothing else, so the only thing that changes between the captures is which page is in front. Its partner page-tint-off proves the same switch leaves the chrome alone when the setting is off - without that pair, this assertion would pass for any repaint at all.

actions.note: let the first tab commit and declare its theme-color
the chrome while the crimson page is in front

actions.expression: (() => { const r = [...document.querySelectorAll('.row.tabrow')].find(x => x.textContent.includes("Teal")); if (!r) return 'no-row'; r.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: Found by title, not by a coordinate the row heights keep moving. the Teal row. A click is the gesture a user makes, and nextTab's cmd+shift+] had no harness key when this was written. Re-measured 2026-08-27 off this scenario's own crimson capture: the sidebar gained a favourites placeholder above the rows since the 2026-08-16 reading of 413, which had been landing in empty sidebar and failing the control below.
the drift is an animation, so it needs longer than a paint
A burst of paints with no navigation and no theme-color change. A per-paint sampler would log through all of it.
the chrome while the teal page is in front
the teal page committed, read from the page itself

assertions.label: the-switch-really-happened
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: the teal page committed, so the measurement below is not grading two captures of the same page. Without it a region that never moved would pass for the wrong reason - the switch never having happened.
THE MEASUREMENT, inverted since the ambilight rework: the sidebar column keeps the space tint across the switch. The page colour lands in the band beside the card only.
assertions.note: Clean sidebar backdrop below the last row and above the dots bar, so no row content moves through the sample.

assertions.label: sampled-per-event-not-per-paint
assertions.desc: The sampler ran a handful of times across two page loads and a scroll burst. A per-paint reader would be in the hundreds. The floor of 1 stops a pattern that matches nothing from satisfying the ceiling. The ceiling was 6 and this run matched exactly 6 - no headroom - once an active-tab change became a third event source alongside a commit and a theme-color change.
The band beside the card follows the page.
assertions.note: Clean sidebar backdrop below the last row and above the dots bar, so no row content moves through the sample.
